name: Extreme wide / extreme long shot (EWS / ELS)
frame_line: whole environment; a person is a small figure (< ~1/8 of frame height)
definition: The place is the subject; people are tiny. Shot scale is defined by the size of the focal subject in the frame (va:CuttingArmstrong2016).
how: Real camera: far away, any lens (wide for space, long for stacked layers). rig.js: cam.set(t,{s:1.0-1.05}). AI: say 'tiny figure' and give the figure's position.
purpose: where/when are we; scale of the world vs the person; loneliness; chapter opening/ending
emotional_effect: awe or isolation depending on light and negative space [CRAFT]
use_when: opening a story or a new location
after a climax, to let the viewer breathe
to make a person small against a problem
avoid_when: the viewer must read a face or a product detail
on a phone feed as the very first frame of a hook (small subject is hard to read at 6 cm wide) [CRAFT]
ai_image_prompt: extreme wide shot, a lone figure small in the lower third of the frame, vast empty beach at dawn, horizon on the upper third, lots of negative space
ai_video_prompt: Extreme wide shot of a vast beach at dawn, a tiny figure walking along the waterline. Locked-off tripod shot, gentle waves, the figure keeps walking left to right.
common_mistakes: no clear focal figure - the eye has nowhere to land
holding it too short: small subjects need longer to find in clutter (va:CuttingArmstrong2016)
check: Can a viewer find the subject in < 1 s on a phone? If not, add contrast/light on it or hold longer.
vertical_9x16: Use height, not width: tall sky or tall street; place the figure on the lower third line.

name: Wide / long shot (WS / LS), establishing
frame_line: full bodies plus a good part of the room/space
definition: Shows people and their geography together; the establishing shot is a wide that sets location and who-is-where before closer coverage.
how: rig.js s 1.0-1.15. Real: 24-35 mm FF-equivalent indoors. AI: 'wide shot, full bodies visible, the whole shop interior'.
purpose: geography, blocking, relationships in space, physical comedy
emotional_effect: more characters per frame correlates with wider scale and longer shots in popular films (Cutting2015-Framing) [EVIDENCE, abstract]
avoid_when: the line or reaction is the point
the background is busy and the subject has no contrast
ai_image_prompt: wide shot of a small optician's shop interior, two people standing at the counter, full bodies visible, eye-level camera, 28mm lens, soft daylight from the window
ai_video_prompt: Wide establishing shot of a small optician's shop. Slow push-in from the doorway toward the counter where two people talk.
common_mistakes: establishing too long in short-form video
characters centred with no depth planes
check: After this shot can the viewer draw a map of who is where and which way they face?
vertical_9x16: Stack depth vertically: foreground at the bottom, subject mid, background top.

name: Full shot (FS)
frame_line: head to feet, little room around
definition: One whole body fills the frame height.
how: rig.js s 1.2-1.4 on the character. AI: 'full-body shot, head to toe in frame, feet visible'.
purpose: body language, posture, costume, entrances, walks
emotional_effect: reads attitude through the whole body [CRAFT]
use_when: a pose tells the story (slumped, proud)
avoid_when: subtle facial acting matters
ai_image_prompt: full-body shot of a young woman in sunglasses standing on a sunlit street, head to toe in frame, feet visible, eye-level, 50mm lens
ai_video_prompt: Full-body shot, a young woman walks toward camera on a sunny street and stops, camera tracks backward with her on a gimbal.
common_mistakes: cutting off the feet at the ankle (awkward joint crop)
camera too high so the legs shrink
check: Are feet and head both inside with a little air? Is the camera near chest-to-waist height?
vertical_9x16: 9:16 is natural for full figures - the body fills the height.

name: Medium wide / medium long / cowboy (MWS / MLS)
definition: Between full and medium: body plus enough face.
how: rig.js s ~1.3-1.5. Name the frame line in prompts ('framed from the knees up') because textbook definitions vary (va cam.cowboy note).
purpose: two people talking while gesturing; hands at hip level; walk-and-talk
avoid_when: the emotional peak of a scene
ai_image_prompt: medium long shot framed from the knees up, two friends talking on a street corner, eye-level, 35mm lens
ai_video_prompt: Medium long shot from the knees up, two friends walk and talk; camera trucks alongside at the same speed, steady.
common_mistakes: frame line on a joint (knee) - go slightly above or below
check: Frame line not on a joint; gestures fully inside.
vertical_9x16: Works for one person; two people side by side get tiny - stagger them in depth.

name: Medium shot (MS)
definition: Waist-up framing; the workhorse of dialogue and presenters.
how: rig.js s 1.5-1.7. Real: 35-50 mm at ~2 m.
avoid_when: you need intimacy or shock
ai_image_prompt: medium shot, waist up, a shop assistant holding a pair of glasses at chest height, looking at camera, eye-level, 50mm lens, soft key light from left
ai_video_prompt: Medium shot, waist up. The shop assistant lifts a pair of glasses toward the camera and smiles. Camera locked off.
common_mistakes: too much headroom
hands cut at the wrist mid-gesture
check: Eyes near the upper third; gestures inside the frame.
vertical_9x16: Default for vertical talking heads; keep the face in the upper third, captions in the safe zone below.

name: Medium close-up (MCU)
definition: Head and shoulders; face readable, some body.
avoid_when: the line is the turning point (save the CU)
ai_image_prompt: medium close-up from the chest up, an older man trying on reading glasses, slight smile, 85mm lens, shallow depth of field, eyes sharp
ai_video_prompt: Medium close-up, an older man puts on reading glasses and blinks, then smiles. Very slow push-in.
common_mistakes: wide lens too close -> nose enlarged (va:BryanPeronaAdolphs2012)
check: Camera at least ~1.5 m away for a natural face (LENS_OPTICS §2).
vertical_9x16: Strongest vertical framing for faces; leave lower 25% for captions.

name: Close-up (CU)
frame_line: face, top of head may be cut
how: rig.js s 2.2-2.6. Real: 85-135 mm from 1.5 m+.
purpose: emotional turns, decisions, the key line
emotional_effect: closeness/intimacy; closer framing increased viewers' mental-state attribution in one study (va:RooneyBalint2018) [EVIDENCE, medium]
facial expressions read faster when larger (va:CuttingArmstrong2016) [EVIDENCE]
use_when: the most important line of a scene
avoid_when: used for every line - it loses force
the character should feel distant or unknowable
ai_image_prompt: close-up of a woman's face, top of the head slightly cropped, tear in one eye, 100mm lens, soft window light, background melted
ai_video_prompt: Close-up of a woman reading a letter; her eyes fill with tears. Slow push-in, locked focus on the eyes.
common_mistakes: spending the CU early
wide lens close (distorts)
huge headroom
check: Is this the beat that deserves the closest shot of the scene?
vertical_9x16: Face fills width; eyes on the upper third.

name: Big close-up / choker (BCU)
frame_line: forehead to chin; hair and jaw cropped
definition: Tighter than CU: only the core of the face (eyes-nose-mouth).
how: rig.js s 2.8-3.2 (puppet line weight grows - check it). Real: 100-135 mm or macro-capable portrait lens.
purpose: pressure, interrogation, intense emotion, Western/standoff stylisation
use_when: peak tension, one or two shots per piece
avoid_when: comedic lightness
with low-resolution AI faces (artefacts become visible)
ai_image_prompt: big close-up, framed from forehead to chin, a man's eyes narrowing, sweat on the brow, 135mm lens, hard side light
ai_video_prompt: Big close-up from forehead to chin; the man's eyes narrow slowly. Camera locked off, no movement.
common_mistakes: AI faces melt at this size - use a real/Codex still + 2.5D push instead
check: Zoom to 100% - are eyes, lashes and skin clean?
vertical_9x16: Crop the sides of the face; eyes still upper third.

name: Extreme close-up (ECU)
frame_line: one feature: an eye, lips, a hinge, a screw
how: Separate insert scene in rig.js (scaling a 1920 bg to s 6 loses resolution). Real: macro lens; AI: 'extreme close-up, macro'.
purpose: shock, detail, clue, sensuality of material
use_when: the plot turns on a detail
avoid_when: the viewer has not yet seen the whole (no context)
ai_image_prompt: extreme close-up macro of a metal eyeglass hinge with a tiny screw, shallow depth of field, specular highlights, dark background
ai_video_prompt: Extreme close-up macro of an eyeglass hinge as it slowly closes. Camera locked off, shallow focus.
common_mistakes: no establishing context before the ECU
AI invents extra screws/temples - check against the real product
check: Does the viewer know what this detail belongs to?

name: Insert
frame_line: an object from the scene fills ~60% of frame
definition: A detail shot of something inside the current scene (letter, receipt, cracked lens).
how: Separate scene/layer; hold long enough to read text twice (GUIDE.md ≥ 2.5 s for short text).
purpose: give the viewer information the plot needs
use_when: text, numbers or a small object carry the plot
avoid_when: the object is already legible in the wider shot
ai_image_prompt: insert shot from above, an optician's prescription card on a wooden counter, a pair of glasses beside it, soft top light, text-free card
ai_video_prompt: Overhead insert of a hand sliding a pair of glasses across a wooden counter. Locked-off overhead shot.
common_mistakes: AI-generated text on the object (house rule: text lives in the HTML layer)
check: Can it be read twice in the hold time?
vertical_9x16: Text-free object; overlay text in HTML inside the safe zone.

name: Cutaway
definition: A shot away from the main action (clock, street, sky) used to compress time or bridge cuts.
how: Any scale; usually a still or slow drift.
purpose: time passage, hiding a cut, adding context or rhythm
use_when: covering a continuity gap between two takes or two AI clips
avoid_when: used as filler without meaning
ai_image_prompt: a wall clock in a quiet shop, late afternoon light, medium close-up, slight dust in the air
ai_video_prompt: Medium close-up of a wall clock; its hands move forward quickly as afternoon light shifts. Locked-off shot.
common_mistakes: cutaway with a different colour grade - breaks continuity
check: Does it carry meaning (time, mood, irony)?
vertical_9x16: Good place to put hook text without covering a face.

name: Two-shot
how: rig.js s 1.1-1.3. Bigger/higher in frame = stronger (GUIDE.md).
purpose: relationship, balance of power, comic timing between two
emotional_effect: togetherness or tension depending on distance between them [CRAFT]
use_when: jokes that need action + reaction in one frame
avoid_when: one character's inner state must dominate
ai_image_prompt: medium two-shot, two friends sitting on a bench facing each other in profile, park at sunset, eye-level, 35mm
ai_video_prompt: Medium two-shot of two friends on a bench; the left one hands the other a gift. Camera locked off, slight breathing drift.
common_mistakes: equal sizes when the story says one dominates
check: Does the staging show who holds the power right now?
vertical_9x16: Stagger in depth (one near, one far) rather than side by side.

name: Over-the-shoulder / dirty single
frame_line: back of A's head/shoulder large in foreground, B facing camera
definition: Dialogue coverage that keeps a piece of the listener in frame.
how: rig.js: foreground layer with A at --d 1.3 (blurred), B on --d 1.0.
purpose: keeps the two characters connected; establishes eyelines and side of the 180° line
avoid_when: the relationship is breaking (switch to clean singles)

examples.note: Gaze-cued cuts establish Rachael-Deckard-owl spatial relations without showing them together; eye-tracking shows viewers' attention follows eyelines across cuts

ai_image_prompt: over-the-shoulder shot, the blurred shoulder and back of a man's head in the left foreground, a woman facing camera across a table, 85mm, shallow depth of field
ai_video_prompt: Over-the-shoulder shot from behind the man; the woman across the table answers him and looks down. Camera locked off.
common_mistakes: foreground shoulder on the wrong side for the established axis (crosses the line)
foreground too big - covers B's face
check: A's shoulder side matches A's screen side in the master.
vertical_9x16: Shoulder at bottom-corner, face upper third.

name: Clean single
frame_line: one character, no part of the other
definition: A single with the other character removed from frame.
how: Same axis and eyeline as the OTS, just without the foreground shoulder.
purpose: isolation; switching dirty -> clean mid-scene says the connection broke (curriculum 05 §1.4)
avoid_when: you want warmth/connection
ai_image_prompt: medium close-up clean single of a woman looking slightly off-camera left, empty dark background, 85mm
ai_video_prompt: Clean single medium close-up; the woman looks off-camera left and slowly turns away. Locked-off shot.
common_mistakes: eyeline pointing the wrong way vs the reverse shot
check: Eyeline direction opposite to the partner's.
vertical_9x16: Look room on the side she looks toward.

name: Point-of-view (POV)
frame_line: what the character sees, at their eye height
definition: The camera takes the character's eye position; best as a 3-shot unit: looker -> POV -> reaction.
how: rig.js: no character on the main layer, cam.drift amp 6-12 + occasional small shake. AI: 'first-person POV, hands visible at the bottom of frame'.
purpose: put the viewer in the character's head; horror; product try-on
use_when: vision demonstrations (blur vs sharp - see lens.myopia_pov_blur)
avoid_when: without the looker shot first (viewer doesn't know whose eyes)
ai_image_prompt: first-person point-of-view, the viewer's hands holding a pair of glasses at the bottom of frame, a blurry street ahead
ai_video_prompt: First-person POV: hands lift a pair of glasses into view and put them on; the blurry street ahead becomes sharp. Slight natural head sway.
common_mistakes: POV height different from the character's height
check: Bracketed by looker and reaction shots?
vertical_9x16: Natural fit - phones are held like a viewfinder.

name: Reaction shot
definition: Shows how a character responds; often more important than the speaker.
how: Cut to the listener on the big line (GUIDE.md); keep eyeline consistent.
purpose: tells the viewer how to feel
emotional_effect: emotion contagion / cueing [CRAFT]; Kuleshov-type context effects - see curriculum 05 caveat
avoid_when: the reaction is predictable and slows pace
ai_image_prompt: medium close-up of a man reacting with stunned surprise, eyebrows raised, looking slightly off-camera right, 85mm
ai_video_prompt: Medium close-up, the man listens, then his eyebrows rise in surprise. Locked-off shot.
common_mistakes: reaction eyeline doesn't point at the speaker's screen position
check: Eyeline matches; held long enough to read the change (~1 s+).

name: Master shot
frame_line: usually WS covering the whole scene action
definition: One continuous shot of the entire scene, into which closer coverage is cut.
how: In rig.js: build the whole scene at s ~1.1, then derive closer 'shots' as camera states on the same stage (cheap coverage).
purpose: safety, geography, a reference for continuity
avoid_when: short-form clips where every second must be close and readable
ai_image_prompt: wide master shot of a family dinner table, all five characters visible, warm practical light, eye-level, 28mm
ai_video_prompt: Wide master shot of a family dinner; everyone talks and passes dishes. Locked-off tripod shot.
common_mistakes: AI cannot give consistent coverage from a master - generate the master as a still and derive crops/2.5D moves from it
check: Every later close shot is consistent with the master (who sits where, light direction).
vertical_9x16: Hard in 9:16; plan vertical coverage instead.

name: Group shot (3+)
definition: Several characters in one frame; staging in depth and triangles keeps it readable.
how: Stagger heights and depths; key figure brightest/sharpest.
emotional_effect: belonging or pressure of the group [CRAFT]
avoid_when: phone screens where faces become too small - cut to singles
ai_image_prompt: group shot of four coworkers in a shop, staggered in depth in a triangle, the manager front and sharpest, 35mm, eye-level
ai_video_prompt: Group shot of four coworkers; they turn together toward the door. Slow push-in.
common_mistakes: everyone in one flat row

name: Foreground shot / dirty frame
frame_line: an out-of-focus object fills part of the frame edge
definition: A near object (shelf, glass, leaves) occupies the foreground; CineScale annotates 'Foreground shot' as its own class.
how: rig.js: fg layer at --d 1.3-1.4 with --blur; it moves fastest in any camera move (parallax).
purpose: depth, voyeurism, frame-within-frame, sells camera movement
use_when: any slow move - foreground parallax makes it read as real
avoid_when: foreground competes in brightness with the subject
ai_image_prompt: shot through blurred eyeglass displays in the foreground, a customer in sharp focus in the midground, 85mm, shallow depth of field
ai_video_prompt: Shot through blurred shelves in the foreground; camera trucks slowly right, the shelves slide past while the customer stays sharp.
common_mistakes: foreground sharp and bright - steals attention
vertical_9x16: Put the foreground element on a side edge or the bottom.
